problems: The Gatherer's straight, separately enclosed thigh pieces read unmistakably as modern shorts, especially on the blue variant. The grass collar does not overcome that underlying clothing read.
The Hearthkeeper resembles a coloured tracksuit with a decorative fur collar. Default sleeves remain enabled, and the long, parallel leg pieces have trouser-like hems.
The Flintworker's smooth diagonal bodice and regular lower tabs need stronger hide construction; the small rectangular tool head reads more like a generic hammer than chipped stone.

The Hearthkeeper and Chief's rounded shoulder pieces read as strings of cream-coloured blobs rather than folded hides. The Chief remains recognisable, but the crowded pale chest ornaments weaken the material read.
The Scout's spear and herder's staff share the arm centreline through much of the upper limb, creating intersection risks. The herder's inward-turning crook also overlaps the hood silhouette.

Several identity details are too small to carry at stream scale: belt stones, basket strips, shell beads and face markings. The herder's hood and luggage communicate travel better than the tiny shell decoration communicates a distinct visiting culture.

Big step up from o1: bare legs, fur-cuff boots, the topknot, the Scout's spear and feather, the Chief's antlers and ochre stripes, and the leader's tusks and shell beads now read as stone age. What still holds the round back is that three of the four everyday kits rely on role-coloured cloth blocks, which keep a modern look.

GATHERER, modern clothes again: the 'hide skirt' is two leg boxes (legL/legR) in pants/pants:dark under a full-torso shirt:dark box. On person 1 that renders as a red tank top over navy-blue denim shorts. It is the most anachronistic thing on the sheet, and the navy is outside the bible palette. Because each leg has its own box, the garment is shorts, not a skirt.

GATHERER, basket: the armL sphere with two cylinder rims and four strut cylinders reads as a drum, tambourine or frying pan held sideways, not a woven gathering basket. The two little green #a8ad68 slats on its front look like dangling tags.

GATHERER, grass cape: from the front only the hips-bone 'collar' shows, four chunky boxes at y≈0.5 that look like a stiff cardboard lei or shoulder pads. The five long cape strips are hidden behind the body. Nothing visible says woven grass.

HEARTHKEEPER, onesie: a shirt:dark torso box, shirt:dark sleeve boxes on both arms and full-length shirt:dark boxes on BOTH legs, finished with a per-leg 'hem', read as a one-piece red (or green) jumpsuit or pyjamas with a belt. The split per-leg hem is trousers, not a robe. This is 'today's clothes recoloured'.

HEARTHKEEPER, chest lumps: the two #c3a575 spheres stacked on the right chest plus the #e1d3ae pin cylinder read as bread rolls or buns glued to the chest, not a folded hide flap. The 'folded shoulder' idea cannot be seen.

FLINTWORKER vs SCOUT: both are bare-chested with a diagonal shoulder strap, a short front flap or loincloth and a stick in the right hand. At stream scale they are the same silhouette, separated only by the spear. The Scout's sash (#987052 box 0.2×0.55 at rotZ 0.35) reads as a plank or quiver board.

FLINTWORKER, tool unreadable: the adze haft (armR cylinder y −0.64, length 0.5) runs down along the forearm and the grey head sits at the hand (y −0.875), tucked beside the thigh. From above it disappears. The #c3a575 'sinew seam' bar (0.45 wide, z 0.18) floats across the belly like a held rod, and the grey sphere and toggle on the belt look like a doorknob.
SCOUT, feather reads as a cigarette: a thin #e1d3ae stick (0.075 wide) topped by a small square #f07835 tip looks exactly like a lit cigarette tucked into the headband.
CHIEF, staff of office: the 'bone top' is a plain #e1d3ae cube on a pole. It reads as a mallet, sledgehammer or blank sign, not a bone or skull finial.

CHIEF, headdress base: the antlers grow out of a flat white box band that reads as a bandage or a paper chef's hat. The two dark-brown vertical slabs standing up behind it read as stray sticks, not feathers.

CHIEF, lower body: shirt/shirt:dark per-leg boxes make brown cargo shorts. The mantle ends at the chest, so apart from the antlers the body is no wider or longer than a resident's. It isn't grand below the shoulders.

LEADER, hood reads as a hard hat: the hat/hat:dark role took the wearer's mustard yellow, and with the flat #e1d3ae brow band plus the forward cone it looks like a yellow construction helmet. A weathered hide hood should be earthy and soft-edged.

LEADER, staff clipping: the hooked staff's crook curls back over and into the hood, so the hook merges with the head silhouette instead of standing clear above it. That is the leader's main 'from far away' cue, and it is lost and visibly clipping.

LEADER, bundle: the hide bundle with the clan emblem is a brown cylinder poking out sideways at hip height behind the right side. It reads as a log or a rolled mat at the hip, and from the front the emblem is invisible.

GLOBAL hair: every kit uses the same flat-topped hair box (y 0.325 lid plus side and back slabs). Every head is a dark square helmet, and the loose versus tied hair the bible asks for barely differs apart from the Flintworker's bun.
fix:
Flintworker of the Sinew Seam: Keep the one-shoulder silhouette and tied hair. Replace the regular lower tabs with three unequal, overlapping hide flaps and give the diagonal wrap one broad folded edge with a few chunky sinew stitches. Make the tool head an asymmetric faceted stone wedge, approximately 25% larger, visibly lashed to its handle.

Overlapping-Grass Gatherer: Remove the shorts-shaped thigh boxes. Build a short, uneven grass-and-hide wrap with overlapping front/back panels and separate leg-bound side flaps; do not bridge both moving legs with one rigid block. Preserve the broad green mantle, but stagger its strip lengths. Simplify the basket to a strong bowl, rim and thick handle visibly held by the hand.

Hearthkeeper in the Folded Shoulder Hide: Add sleeves to the hide list and replace the narrow custom sleeve boxes with short, irregular hide shoulder coverings. Rebuild the lower garment as an overlapping, split hide apron with unequal leg-bound side panels rather than two trouser tubes. Replace the shoulder spheres with broad faceted folds, leaving one prominent fastening and a clear pale shoulder silhouette.

Young Ridge Scout: Preserve the exposed torso, narrow pelt and feather. Move the spear shaft outward from the arm centreline to a visible hand grip, then angle it away from the shoulder. Use a chipped, asymmetric stone point with a substantial binding; retain the compact loincloth rather than adding shorts.

Chief of the Great Branched Antlers: Keep the antler crown and raised staff as the primary office symbols. Replace the round fur clusters with a broad, angular shoulder pelt; simplify the chest decoration to three large teeth on a visible cord. Give the lower hide an irregular overlapping hem. Shape the staff's ivory block into a recognisable bone or animal-head emblem with one large dark recess.

Far-Roving Shell-Cowl Mammoth Herder: Keep the enclosing hood, patchwork hide and bedroll. Replace the bead row with three larger shell clusters repeated on the hood and pack, making the visiting culture readable from above. Move the staff outside the arm and turn its hook outward so it clears the hood. Make the paired tusk ornaments visibly attached to a hide yoke. Check every kit in walking poses at the actual 40-degree gameplay camera and final stream size. / GATHERER: delete the two leg boxes and the pants waist box. Add ONE hips skirt box at [0,-0.12,0], size [0.50,0.36,0.32], colour #987052 (hide never varies), plus 3–4 thin #76513b ragged hem tabs at y -0.30. Replace the torso shirt:dark box with a sleeveless wrap in #c3a575 or #987052, and use the shirt role only for a small accent. Make the grass cape the front silhouette: a hips-bone shoulder cape of 5–6 overlapping, downward-tapering #a8ad68/#7c9254/#c3a575 slabs, 0.08 deep, hanging from y 0.58 to y 0.25 so they drape over the chest and upper arms, rotated outwards ±0.25 so they flare. Drop the stiff blocks. Basket: on armL make an upright open-top cone (point down) at [0,-0.62,0.05], size [0.26,0.30,0.26], colour #c3a575, with two #76513b cylinder bands around it, a single arched #76513b handle up to the hand, and a few #7c9254 leaf tips poking out of the top. No flat disc.

HEARTHKEEPER: remove the sleeve boxes (hide sleeves) and all four leg boxes. Make it a long robe: one hips box [0,0.08,0] size [0.50,1.0,0.32] tapering to a second wider skirt box [0,-0.38,0] size [0.56,0.36,0.36], both #987052/#76513b hide (role only on the belt or trim), ending at mid-calf over bare shins. Replace the chest buns with a real one-shoulder fold: a #c3a575 box [0.12,0.42,0.02] size [0.30,0.40,0.34] rotZ -0.35 lapping over the left shoulder, plus a fur collar ring of 3 #e1d3ae spheres. Keep the gourd. Give the hair a long braid down the back so the head differs.

FLINTWORKER: keep the bun and the one-shoulder wrap, but make the wrap hide (#987052) over a short kilt, and drop the floating 'seam' bar and doorknob sphere. Make the adze a big read: the haft held vertically up from the hand on armR (cylinder at [0,-0.25,0.05] length 0.9), with the grey #81847a head as a 0.28×0.10×0.12 box lashed crosswise at the TOP above shoulder height, plus a #c3a575 lashing box. Add a leather work apron (#76513b, front only, y -0.05 to -0.40) so this kit is 'worker with apron + raised adze', unlike the Scout.

SCOUT: keep it bare-chested with the loincloth and spear, but replace the plank sash with a thin cord sash (0.05 wide) holding a small pouch, and add a short #987052 fur shoulder cape (cape bone, size [0.46,0.35,0.04]) so its back silhouette differs. Feather: make it 0.10 wide tapering (a cone or rotated box) in #e1d3ae with a #526b40 or #76513b mid-band and a slanted #f07835 tip, angled 0.4 rad outwards. Not a white stick with an orange end.

CHIEF: make the staff finial an animal skull. A #e1d3ae sphere [0.20,0.16,0.22] plus two small cones as horns, or two eye-socket #76513b boxes, sitting on the pole top, with a fur wrap ring below it. Replace the white band under the antlers with a #987052 fur cap (sphere, slightly larger than the head top) with a #e1d3ae browband 0.04 tall. Turn the two dark slabs into 3 real feathers (thin tapered boxes #e1d3ae/#f07835, splayed). Replace the per-leg shorts with one long layered hide skirt (hips, [0.56,0.50,0.36] at y -0.20) and extend the mantle into a wide pelt: cape bone box [0.62,0.95,0.06] in #76513b, with #e1d3ae fur trim spheres at the shoulders sticking out 0.08 past the arms, so the Chief is visibly wider and longer than residents from above.

LEADER: stop using the hat role for the hood. Use fixed #76513b/#987052 with a ragged #c3a575 fur edge round the face opening, and round the top (a sphere instead of the forward cone) so it can't read as a hard hat. Move the hooked staff to the right hand, standing outside the body (armR, pole length 1.9 so the crook sits 0.35 m above the hood and 0.25 m out to the side). The crook should be two short angled cylinders that curl away from the head and never pass over it. Put the hide bundle on the back as a big rolled pack (cape bone, a cylinder laid horizontally across the shoulders, [0.55,0.2,0.2], #987052), with a bold 2-colour #4d9495/#e9b04c emblem box (0.16 square) on its visible end, so 'from far away' reads from above. Keep the shell beads and tusks. Give the patchwork wrap at least 3 clearly different fur tones in large patches.

GLOBAL: vary the head silhouettes per kit (bun, long braid, loose hair falling past the shoulders as two side slabs to y -0.05, a shaved or fur-band head), so the dark square helmet stops repeating. Keep role colours for small personal accents only (a belt, a band, a skirt panel), never for whole torso or leg boxes.
